channel.title: ARAD Networks Insights
channel.description: From network architecture to AI infrastructure and connectivity in the field. Questions that help us design and operate connections.

item.title: Where does network separation begin?
item.description: Start by understanding how devices communicate, not just what devices exist.
item.content:encoded:
From inventory to relationships

A name and an IP address do not describe a device’s communication needs. Its services, ownership and remote access requirements are the starting points for defining boundaries.

Shared infrastructure, different purposes

A camera communicating with a monitoring server has different requirements from an employee workstation. Separation is about defining required communication, rather than removing every connection.

Tunnels and routing spaces

ARAD’s SPN combines per-device tunnels with separate routing spaces. It defines individual paths and permitted destinations through policy. This does not automatically replace encryption or other security controls.

What to establish first

Prepare communication maps, equipment details, change constraints and rollout requirements. Include ongoing management and maintenance in the evaluation.

item.title: Why look at GPUs and networks together?
item.description: Data movement between computation steps is part of understanding AI workload performance.
item.content:encoded:
The time between computation

AI workloads include data movement and communication as well as computation. Congestion and queues in shared networks can affect performance, but networking is not the cause of every delay.

Logical paths and transmission queues

Separating routing domains and managing hardware transmission queues are related challenges. ARAD is evaluating how AMLI links logical workload paths to hardware queues.

Compare under controlled conditions

Throughput and latency comparisons require controlled workloads, data sizes, concurrency, switch configurations and measurement intervals. Conditions matter as much as the resulting numbers.

Current evaluation status

AMLI performance effects are under validation. GPU utilisation gains and throughput improvements are not claimed at this stage. Evaluation begins by defining the operating environment and measurement criteria.

item.title: Three things to assess before choosing site connectivity
item.description: Space, existing infrastructure and operating needs guide the choice of connectivity.
item.content:encoded:
Space and movement

Above-ground areas, underground spaces, open rooms and winding corridors have different connectivity conditions. Begin with device mobility and where data is generated.

Existing infrastructure

Power lines, network cabling and wireless equipment form the starting point. PLC uses power lines for data communication, but wiring and electrical conditions must be evaluated.

Operations and maintenance

Device count, data requirements and maintenance procedures also matter. Wi-Fi mesh placement and private 5G design should follow these operating needs.

Combine technologies around conditions

ARAD evaluates private 5G, Wi-Fi mesh and PLC around site conditions. Deployment requirements come before treating a technology’s maximum specification as on-site performance.
